extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of classical Euclidean geometry; readers of Euclid's Data
extracted.subtask_description: Propositions from Euclid's Data that state when geometric objects (points, lines, angles, ratios, triangles, figures) are 'given' in position, magnitude, or species, and constructive/decision procedures showing how to obtain the remaining objects. These are constructive criteria used in classical plane geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXX — extremity of a given line
rubrics_metrics.description: If one of the extremities of a straight line given in position and magnitude be given, the other extremity shall also be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given point A and a straight line AC given in position and magnitude which contains the other extremity: construct from AC a segment equal to the given magnitude (use defn. of equality); cutting AC at the equal length identifies B, the other extremity. Any other point on the same side would cut off a different length, so B is uniquely determined. Also a symmetric point can be found on the other side of A by producing AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXXI — line through given point parallel to given line
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be drawn through a given point parallel to a straight line given in position; that straight line is given in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through given point A draw the unique straight line (by construction) parallel to BC which is given in position. Because no other line through A is parallel to BC, the constructed line has an invariable position and therefore is given in position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXXII — line to a given point in a given line making given angle
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be drawn to a given point in a straight line given in position, and makes a given angle with it; that straight line is given in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given line AB (position) and point C on it. Given angle can be copied at C to form angle ECB equal to the given one; that determines the straight line EC. Any other line through C would make a different angle with CB, so EC is fixed in position. Note there are two such lines (one on each side) giving equal angles when produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXXIII — line from a given point to a given line making given angle
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be drawn from a given point to a straight line given in position, and makes a given angle with it, that straight line is given in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From given point A draw AD to given line (position) so that angle ADC equals the given angle. Construct through A a line parallel to the given line, use equal angles from intersecting parallels to deduce the required angle is given; hence AD has fixed position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXXIV — given magnitude from point to given line implies given position
rubrics_metrics.description: If from a given point to a straight line given in position, a straight line be drawn which is given in magnitude; the same is also given in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given point A, line BC (position), and a segment of a given magnitude from A to BC. Compare that magnitude to the perpendicular AE from A to BC (shortest distance). If the given magnitude equals AE, AE is the unique such segment and so is given in position. If not equal, produce AE and construct circle centered at A with radius equal to the given magnitude; intersection(s) with BC are points at the given distance and are determined by intersections of given-position objects (circle and line), hence their positions are fixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXXV — line between parallels with given angles is given in magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be drawn between two parallel straight lines given in position, and makes given angles with them, the straight line is given in magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given parallels AB and CD in position and a line EF between them making given angles with the parallels. Take a given point on CD and draw through it a line parallel to EF; using equality of alternate/ corresponding angles, one constructs a segment GH between parallels equal in magnitude; since points H and G are determined the segment GH is given; EF equals GH hence EF is given in magnitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXXVI — given magnitude between parallels yields given angles
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line given in magnitude be drawn between two parallel straight lines given in position, it shall make given angles with the parallels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given EF of known magnitude between parallels AB and CD. Construct a segment G equal to EF, use a given point H on AB and drop perpendicular HK to CD to compare minimal distances; by considering equality/inequality with perpendicular, produce circle(s) and use intersections with given-position objects to locate points M,N. From those, construct a line EO parallel to one of the constructed segments, deduce EF makes the same (hence given) angle(s) with the parallels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXXVII — from given magnitude to line in given angle, parallel through point is given in position
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line given in magnitude be drawn from a point to a straight line given in position, in a given angle; the straight line drawn through that point parallel to the straight line given in position, is given in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given AD (magnitude) from point A to line EC (position) in given angle ADC; pick a given point on BC and draw a line parallel to AD. That constructed GH is given in both position and magnitude; knowing one extremity yields the other, hence the line through the relevant point parallel to BC is fixed in position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXXVIII — ratio of segments from point to two parallels is given
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be drawn from a given point to two parallel straight lines given in position, the ratio of the segments between the given point and the parallels shall be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From point E draw EF and EG to parallels AB and CD. Drop perp EK to CD (given in position); the perpendiculars produce fixed points H,K so EH and EK are given in magnitude, hence their ratio is given. By similarity (parallelism), ratio EF:EG equals EH:EK, so EF:EG is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXXIX — if ratio of segments from point to parallels given and one parallel's position given, the other parallel's position is given
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ratio of the segments of a straight line between a given point in it and two parallel straight lines be given, if one of the parallels be given in position, the other is also given in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given point A on line AED with AE:AD ratio known, and BC (one parallel) given in position. Drop AH perpendicular to BC, locate H (given); using proportionality produce AK such that AK:AH equals AE:AD; locate K (given in magnitude and position). Through K draw line parallel to EC (given in position) to obtain FG, the other parallel, which is then fixed in position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XL — third parallel determined by two given parallels and given segment ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ratio of the segments of a straight line into which it is cut by three parallel straight lines be given; if two of the parallels are given in position, the third also is given in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given AB and CD in position and the ratio in which they cut line GEF; take a given point L on AB, draw LM perpendicular to CD meeting HK at N. Using given ratios and LM (given in magnitude & position), determine LN (hence N). Through N draw HK parallel to CD (given in position) to obtain the third parallel; the construction uses only given-position/magnitude objects so HK is fixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XLI — segments cut by three given parallels have a given ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line meets three parallel straight lines which are given in position, the segments into which they cut it have a given ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take given point L on AB and draw LM perpendicular to CD meeting EF at N. LM and MN are determined (given in magnitude), so their ratio is given; since by geometry GH:HK = LM:MN, the ratio of GH to HK (segments cut by the parallels on the transversal) is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XLII — triangle with all sides given in magnitude is given in species
rubrics_metrics.description: If each of the sides of a triangle be given in magnitude, the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct triangle DEF with sides equal respectively to given AB, BC, CA (possible because any two exceed the third). Then corresponding angles are equal (by side-side-side) so triangle ABC's angles are determined (given). Ratios of sides are known, hence triangle is given in species (shape up to congruence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XLIII — triangle with all angles given in magnitude is given in species
rubrics_metrics.description: If each of the angles of a triangle be given in magnitude, the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take a line DE given in position and magnitude, construct at D and E angles equal to BAC and ABC; the third angles are equal as result. Draw FD to meet requirements; FD, DE, EF become given in position and magnitude, so triangle DEF is determined and similar to ABC; thus ABC is given in species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XLIV — one angle and ratio of adjacent sides determine triangle species
rubrics_metrics.description: If one of the angles of a triangle be given, and if the sides about it have a given ratio to one another; the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given angle BAC and ratio BA:AC. Construct DE (given in position & magnitude) and make angle at D equal to BAC, then set ED:DF equal to BA:AC so DF is determined in magnitude; since FD is drawn to a given point D in a given position angle, FD is given in position. Points determined yield triangle DEF given in species and similar to ABC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XLV — triangle whose sides have given ratios is given in species
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sides of a triangle have to one another given ratios, the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a line D of given magnitude; using given ratios create segments E and F so D:E:F reflect AB:BC:CA. Show any two of D,E,F exceed the third so triangle GHK with sides equal to D,E,F exists; as ratios match those of ABC, triangles are equiangular and similar, and since constructed triangle is given in species, so is ABC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XLVI — right triangle with given adjacent-side ratio is given in species
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sides of a right-angled triangle about one of the acute angles have a given ratio to one another; the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given ratio AB:BC in right triangle ABC. Construct DE:EF equal to AB:BC with DE given. Draw DO perpendicular to DE and construct circle with centre E radius EF meeting DG; intersections yield points making triangle DEG determined (given in species). Triangles ABC and DEG are similar with all sides/angles determined, so ABC is given in species. Both possible intersections give two such triangles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XLVII — one non-right angle and ratio about another angle determine triangle species
rubrics_metrics.description: If a triangle has one of its angles which is not a right angle given, and if the sides about another angle have a given ratio to one another; the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle cases depending on whether the ratio is equality, less-to-greater or greater-to-less: construct DE (given) with angle equal to the given angle and set ED:DG according to ratio, then use circle intersections to obtain triangles DEF (one or two possibilities). Using comparisons with right angles and similarity arguments show ABC is similar to a constructed triangle given in species; sometimes two distinct species can satisfy the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XLVIII — given angle and ratio of sum of two sides to third determines triangle species
rubrics_metrics.description: If a triangle has one angle given, and if both the sides together about that angle have a given ratio to the remaining side; the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bisect the given angle to get AD; reduce the condition to a ratio AB:BD which is given. With the angle BAD given and the ratio AB:BD given, triangle ABD is determined in species; from that deduce the rest of ABC is given in species. Construction method is described to actually build such a triangle from given data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XLIX — one angle given plus ratio of two adjacent sides together to third determines triangle species
rubrics_metrics.description: If a triangle has one angle given, and if the sides about another angle, both together, have a given ratio to the third side; the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bisect the relevant angle reducing to proposition XLIV/XLVIII arguments: the ratio of BA and AC together to BC gives AB:BD (via bisector), so triangle ABD is given in species; doubling angles yields full triangle ABC determined. Construction steps provided to find the required triangle from given angle and ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. L — cevian from vertex in given species triangle has given ratio to base
rubrics_metrics.description: If from the vertex of a triangle given in species, a straight line be drawn to the base in a given angle; it shall have a given ratio to the base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In triangle ABC given in species, draw AD to base BC in given angle ADB. Because triangle ABD is given in species, AD:AB ratio is given, and AB:BC is given (species fixes ratios), hence AD:BC is determined (composition of given ratios).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. LI — rectilineal figure given in species can be divided into triangles given in species
rubrics_metrics.description: Rectilineal figures given in species are divided into triangles which are given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given polygon ABCDE in species: join diagonals BE, BD, etc. Angles formed (e.g. BAE) are given; using those given angles and ratios, each resulting triangle is determined in species. The proposition shows how to partition a figure given in species into constituent triangles each also given in species.
